item_arguments.definition_or_claim: Let V→X be an oriented Euclidean real vector bundle of rank n, with oriented frame bundle P_SO(V). Use Spin(n)=Spin_full(ℝⁿ,−‖·‖²), the full even subgroup of the negative-square Pin group, and its standard twisted-Clifford homomorphism λ_n:Spin(n)→SO(n). A Spin structure on V is a principal Spin(n)-bundle P with a Spin(n)-equivariant two-fold map P→P_SO(V) covering the identity on X and compatible with λ_n. A Spin^c structure is a principal Spin^c(n) lift of P_SO(V), where Spin^c(n)=(Spin(n)×U(1))/⟨(−1,−1)⟩. A spinor bundle is the associated bundle for the specified real Clifford representation; a Spin^c spinor bundle uses the specified complex representation and its U(1) weight. These are given structures; this definition asserts no existence criterion.

numbered_steps.text: If $X=\varnothing$, the conclusion is vacuous; assume $X$ is nonempty. For each $i$ define the $i$th component of $\Phi:E\to X\times\mathbb R^{rs}$ over $x$ by $\sqrt{\rho_i(x)}\tau_i(v)$ when $x\in U_i$, and by zero when $x\notin U_i$. The real square-root function is continuous on $[0,\infty)$ (away from zero, $|\sqrt a-\sqrt b|=|a-b|/(\sqrt a+\sqrt b)$; at zero, $0\le\sqrt a<\varepsilon$ whenever $0\le a<\varepsilon^2$). Because $\operatorname{supp}(\rho_i)\subseteq U_i$, every point outside $U_i$ has a neighborhood on which $\rho_i=0$; hence extending the chart component by zero is continuous there, and within $U_i$ it is a product of continuous coordinate functions. Hence each component, and therefore $\Phi$, is continuous. It is fiberwise linear. [given, F1, F2, construct]

If $v\in E_x$ is nonzero, the partition identity gives some $i$ with $\rho_i(x)>0$. Then $x\in U_i$ and [F1] makes $\tau_i(v)\ne0$, so the $i$th component of $\Phi_x(v)$ is nonzero. Thus each $\Phi_x$ is injective and has rank $r$. [given, F1, step 1.1, algebra]

In local bundle coordinates, the matrix of $\Phi$ has rank $r$ at every point. At any chosen $x$, some $r\times r$ minor is nonzero; continuity keeps that minor nonzero on a neighborhood. After reordering the target coordinates, the image there is the graph of a continuous matrix over $\mathbb R^r$. Thus $E'=\Phi(E)$ is a rank-$r$ subbundle of the trivial bundle. [step 2.1, algebra]

On a neighborhood with a continuous frame matrix $Q$ for $E'$, the orthogonal projection onto $E'$ is $P=Q(Q^{\mathsf T}Q)^{-1}Q^{\mathsf T}$. The Gram matrix $Q^{\mathsf T}Q$ is positive definite and invertible; its inverse varies continuously because each inverse entry is a cofactor divided by the nonzero determinant, so $P$ is continuous. Therefore $I-P$ has locally constant rank $rs-r$ and its image is a subbundle $F=E'^{\perp}$. Fiberwise orthogonal decomposition gives $E'\oplus F=X\times\mathbb R^{rs}$, and $\Phi$ identifies $E$ with $E'$. If $r=0$, take $E'=0$ and $F=X\times\mathbb R^0$. [step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra] ∎

numbered_steps.text: In an oriented orthonormal frame the generators anticommute and each has square $-1$. Reversing the product order takes $n(n-1)/2=2m(4m-1)$ swaps, an even number; multiplying the $n$ generator squares contributes $(-1)^{4m}=1$. Thus $\omega^2=1$. For any orthonormal frame, pairwise anticommutation makes the product equal to the alternating product $\operatorname{Alt}(v_1,\ldots,v_n)=\frac1{n!}\sum_\sigma\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)c(v_{\sigma(1)})\cdots c(v_{\sigma(n)})$. This is an alternating multilinear function of the frame vectors. An oriented orthogonal change has determinant $+1$, so it leaves this top alternating product unchanged. Hence $\omega$ is frame-independent and, in local frames, varies continuously. [given, F2, algebra]

Moving any unit vector $v$ past the other $n-1$ orthogonal generators gives $\omega c(v)=(-1)^{n-1}c(v)\omega=-c(v)\omega$. Since $n$ is even, $\omega$ has even parity, so it preserves $\Lambda^0$ and $\Lambda^1$. The continuous maps $p_\pm=(I\pm\omega)/2$ are idempotents with $p_+p_-=0$ and $p_++p_-=I$. In any local frame their matrix entries vary continuously, and the trace of an idempotent equals its rank, so each image rank is locally constant. At a point choose a basis of the image; applying $p_\pm$ to the same frame vectors remains independent on a neighborhood and spans the image there. Thus their images are complementary graded subbundles. The anticommutation identity makes $c(v)$ interchange their images, and $c(v)^{-1}=-c(v)$ for $\lVert v\rVert=1$, so the interchange is an isomorphism. [given, F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

Pull the two eigenbundles back to the two closed disk halves of $S(\mathbb R\oplus V)$. Thicken the halves slightly so their overlap is an equatorial collar; radial projection in each fiber identifies that collar continuously with $S(V)$, so extend the transition $c(v)$ constantly along the radial coordinate. The opposite transition is $-c(v)$, its inverse, and the two-chart cocycle is therefore satisfied. The quotient gluing theorem [F4] gives a vector bundle, and its relative disk/sphere triple is exactly $(\Lambda^+,c(v),\Lambda^-)$. The volume eigenspaces are defined by $\omega$, whereas parity is the grading operator in [F1]; these are distinct constructions, and no identification between them is assumed. [F1, F3, F4, step 2.1, construct] ∎
